what_its_for: Ciclopirox olamine is an antifungal medicine used to treat fungal skin infections. This includes athlete's foot (tinea pedis), jock itch (tinea cruris), ringworm (tinea corporis), and a skin condition called tinea versicolor that causes discolored patches on the skin. It works by stopping the growth of the fungus causing your infection.
how_to_take: This medicine is applied directly to the skin (topical use only). Clean and dry the affected area completely before applying. Use a thin layer of the cream, gel, or lotion and gently rub it in. Wash your hands before and after applying, unless your hands are the area being treated. Do not cover the area with a bandage or wrap unless your doctor tells you to. For nail lacquer (Penlac), apply it like nail polish directly onto the affected nail and surrounding skin. For shampoo (Stieprox), wet your hair, apply to scalp, lather, and leave on for 3 to 5 minutes before rinsing. Do not get this medicine in your eyes, nose, or mouth. If contact occurs, rinse well with water.
dosing: For cream, gel, or lotion: Apply to the affected area twice daily (morning and evening) for 2 to 4 weeks, or as directed by your doctor. For nail lacquer: Apply once daily at bedtime or 8 hours before washing for up to 48 weeks. For shampoo: Use twice a week for 4 weeks, with at least 3 days between each use. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may vary depending on your condition.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not apply a double dose to make up for the one you missed. Try to apply this medicine at the same times each day to help you remember.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep the lid or cap tightly closed when not in use. Keep away from heat, direct sunlight, and open flame. Do not freeze this medication. Keep out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the packaging.
what_to_avoid: Avoid getting this medicine in your eyes, nose, mouth, or vagina. Do not use on open wounds or severely irritated skin unless directed by your doctor. Avoid wearing tight, synthetic clothing or non-breathable socks over the treated area, as this can make your infection worse. For nail lacquer, avoid using nail polish or other nail products on the treated nails. Avoid sharing towels, shoes, or socks with others while you have an infection, as it can spread to others.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor if you notice any of the following: severe skin irritation, redness, burning, swelling, or blistering at the application site that was not there before; signs of a new or worsening infection; no improvement in your condition after 4 weeks of treatment (or 48 weeks for nail lacquer); signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, difficulty breathing, or swelling of the face, lips, or throat. Seek emergency medical help right away if you have a serious allergic reaction.
when_it_works: You may start to notice improvement within 2 to 4 weeks of regular use. However, it is very important to keep using this medicine for the full length of time prescribed, even if you feel better or the infection looks gone. Stopping too early can allow the fungus to come back. Nail infections take the longest to improve and may require several months of treatment before full results are seen.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Use only if your doctor determines the benefit outweighs any potential risk. Children: The safety of ciclopirox in children under 10 years old has not been fully established. Consult your doctor before using in young children. Older adults: No special dose adjustment is usually needed, but older skin may be more sensitive. Let your doctor know if irritation occurs. People with diabetes or poor circulation: Use extra caution when applying nail lacquer and discuss risks with your doctor, especially regarding skin around the nails.
